message.content:
The given statements describe a collection of ancestor/descendant relationships that can be represented as a directed acyclic graph with edges of the form \(A > B\) ("\(A\) is an ancestor of \(B\)").

Chaining the edges yields a single connected component containing (among many others) the following two paths that share a prefix:

- Jacob > Eric > Diane > Dorothy > … > Kayla > Susan  
- Jacob > Amber > Laura > … > Stephanie > Judith > Hannah  

Thus Jacob (and every node that reaches Jacob) lies on an ancestor path to both Susan and Hannah.  

Neither Susan nor Hannah lies on any path reaching the other, so one is not an ancestor of the other. The two paths diverge after Jacob and never reconverge, so Susan and Hannah have no common descendant.

The only relationship that holds is therefore that Susan and Hannah share a common ancestor.

<ANSWER>2</ANSWER>
